subject: PD brief 19 – 26 Nov 2026: 53 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days were dominated by prehospital sepsis trials that found no benefit from liberal fluids or ambulance antibiotics, alongside a steady run of cardiac arrest papers on bystander action, AEDs and prognosis. Trauma also featured strongly, with a Cochrane-quality review supporting prehospital TXA.
synthesis.discussion: Given two large trials found no benefit from prehospital fluids or antibiotics in suspected sepsis, where do you and your partner think the real survival gains lie for these patients — earlier recognition, faster transport, or something else entirely?

lessons.text: Two large paramedic-led trials found no mortality benefit from liberal prehospital fluids (median 1500 mL vs 500 mL) or IM ceftriaxone in suspected sepsis — a reminder that usual care with an early hospital handover remains a defensible approach for these patients.

A systematic review of randomised trials supports current practice on prehospital TXA for bleeding trauma: lower 28–30-day mortality with no significant increase in thromboembolic events or seizures, though the TBI signal rests on a single trial.

Bystander-attached AEDs were linked with far better OHCA survival (28% vs around 9% for EMS-attached), and shockable rhythms decay fast with time-to-defibrillation — so coaching bystanders to grab and attach the nearest AED early is one of the highest-value things you can do on scene.

In paediatric OHCA, registry data suggest rescue breaths matter: bystander CPR with rescue breaths was linked with better neurological survival than compression-only CPR in children — worth remembering when a bystander asks what to do for a child in arrest.

Choking-related arrests achieved prehospital ROSC far more often than cardiac arrests (62.7% vs 37.8%), but survival stayed similar and remained poor without ROSC — persistent airway management effort on scene is reasonable, yet conversations about outcomes should stay realistic.

deep_dives.why: Two large factorial RCTs found no benefit from either liberal fluids or prehospital antibiotics in suspected sepsis, and their entry criteria (fever plus SBP under 100) exclude the sickest patients — worth unpacking against your local sepsis pathway.
questions: How does your local sepsis pathway compare with the trial's entry criteria of fever plus SBP under 100 mmHg?
Given hospital antibiotics arrived within about 4 hours of paramedic arrival for most trial patients, what does that say about where your effort is best spent?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the trial populations with the sepsis patients you actually transport, and consider which patients the fever-plus-hypotension criteria excluded. Look at where prehospital time is saved or lost in your local pathway against the trial's ~4-hour antibiotic gap.

deep_dives.why: Several papers converge on the same lever: bystander action before we arrive is tied to the biggest survival differences in OHCA, and app-based first responder alerts were linked with more bystander defibrillation and a small survival gain.
questions: How do you currently coach bystanders to attach an AED while you are still en route or arriving?
The self-efficacy study suggests confidence, not attitude, drives bystander willingness — does that change how you would explain CPR to a hesitant bystander?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the survival gap between bystander and EMS-attached AEDs with the confounding caveat that early recognition drives both, and consider whether app-based alerts exist in your catchment. Look at how your local GoodSAM-style system is activated and where the gaps are.

deep_dives.why: Paediatric papers from this period challenge two assumptions: compression-only CPR may not serve children, and an updated US position statement reshapes thinking on paediatric traumatic arrest management.
questions: Would you coach rescue breaths over compression-only CPR for a child, and how does that sit with your local guideline?
The position statement recommends chest decompression only when thoracic trauma is suspected — does that match how you currently approach paediatric traumatic arrest?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the position statement's airway and decompression recommendations with your local guideline, noting it is US consensus rather than Australian guidance. Consider why adrenaline was given before transport in only 41% of non-shockable paediatric arrests in the US cohort.

papers.title: Prehospital TXA lowers mortality in bleeding trauma
papers.design: Systematic review with meta-analysis restricted to randomised trials (Cochrane RoB2)
papers.n: 21 reports; 3 randomised trials pooled for mortality (PATCH-Trauma, STAAMP, ROC-TXA)
papers.finding: Lower 28–30-day mortality with prehospital TXA (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68–0.95); TBI mortality (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.64–1.20) and in-hospital mortality came from single trials; no statistically significant increase in thromboembolic events or seizures.

papers.title: Bystander-attached AEDs linked with best OHCA survival
papers.design: Registry-based cohort study (EMS, dispatch and registry linkage)
papers.finding: EMS attached the first AED in 72% of cases; 30-day survival was 28% with bystander attachment vs 9.0% EMS, 8.7% on-duty first responders and 8.6% community first responders; bystander attachment associated with higher 30-day survival (OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.77–2.85), rising to 62% in witnessed shockable arrests.

papers.title: First responder alerts linked to more defibrillation
papers.design: Registry linkage cohort (cardiac arrest registry, AED network, app data) with TMLE
papers.finding: Activation (41% of cases) predicted bystander defibrillation of 9.6% vs 5.5% at 389 m and 13.0% vs 4.8% at 1,183 m; TMLE estimated +6.1 pp bystander defibrillation (95% CI 4.5–7.8) and +1.8 pp 30-day survival (95% CI 0.1–3.6).

papers.title: Mobile app lifts simulated trauma performance
papers.design: Crossover randomised controlled trial, high-fidelity simulation
papers.n: 48 paramedic pairs analysed (112 recruited), adult and paediatric trauma scenarios
papers.finding: 35.4% of app-supported scenarios met all critical actions vs 6.3% without (adjusted OR 8.28, 95% CI 2.21–31.09); paediatric completion 30.4% vs 0%; users rated the app practical and valuable.

papers.title: Prehospital STEMI thrombolysis is value for money
papers.design: Decision-analytic microsimulation model (health-provider perspective, lifetime horizon)
papers.n: Modelled cohort from all QAS STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis, 2022–2024
papers.finding: AUD 16,750 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range 15,477–18,423), equivalent to USD 11,725; results robust in sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Five years of automated head-up CPR outcomes
papers.design: Prospective observational multicentre registry study
papers.n: 3,709 adults with non-traumatic OHCA across 10 US EMS agencies serving 1.5 million people
papers.finding: ROSC 29.5%, survival to discharge 13.1%, favourable neurological survival 10.5%; shockable rhythm 33.9% favourable survival vs 2.0% asystole; 91% of the 391 survivors had CPC 1.

papers.title: MIRA-29: early prehospital prognosis after arrest
papers.design: Prospective derivation cohort with external registry validation
papers.n: 1,099 derivation patients plus 82,696 external validation patients
papers.finding: Low-flow duration, shock count, adrenaline dose and arrest site predicted neurological outcome; precision 0.86 and recall 0.88 in external validation, specificity for poor outcome 0.99; age was not retained in the final model.

papers.title: Digital support pathway for OHCA bystanders feasible
papers.design: Prospective one-year regional service evaluation
papers.n: 432 eligible OHCA incidents; 260 adult bystanders registered
papers.finding: Incident-level capture 50.9%; 96.2% of registered adults accessed digital resources at least once; ~10% self-referred for liaison officer support; 10.1% of identified bystanders were under 18; EMS clinicians rated it acceptable.

papers.title: Video calls showed no clear resource savings
papers.design: Post hoc analysis of a cluster-randomised trial
papers.finding: Initial dispatch 69.4% vs 73.9% (risk difference −4.5 pp, 95% CI −10.0 to 1.0); cumulative unit time −1.5 min (95% CI −6.2 to 3.1); no outcome reached statistical significance and later dispatch didn't offset the difference.

papers.title: Neonatal chest compressions: most survive a month
papers.design: Retrospective population-based cohort (perinatal data collection)
papers.finding: 70.5% established regular breathing within 60 minutes and 89.0% survived to 28 days; adjusted survival odds fell with gestational age (aOR 0.17 under 28 weeks), though the term vs moderate-preterm gap attenuated after adjusting for cord pH or adrenaline.

papers.title: Chinese OHCA registry: low survival, low AED use
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of a prospective Utstein-style province-wide EMS registry
papers.finding: 30-day survival 3.0%, favourable neurological outcome 2.0%; bystander CPR 47.7%, dispatcher-assisted CPR 20.0%, bystander AED use 1.8%; shockable rhythm the strongest factor for survival and neurological recovery; survival declined with longer EMS response times.

papers.title: OHCA cause attribution shifts with definitions
papers.design: Retrospective registry linkage study (bootstrap cluster CIs)
papers.finding: Cardiac attribution estimates ranged from 20.74% to 42.32% across the definition matrix; in paired records, registry-recorded cardiac attribution was 22.70% vs 27.82% under a broader rule (difference 5.12 pp, 95% CI 0.96–8.51).

papers.title: Clinician smartphones linked to tripled interpreter use
papers.design: Retrospective pre-post observational cohort
papers.n: 430 interpreter requests across pre- and post-implementation periods
papers.finding: Requests rose from 104 (0.19 per 100 encounters) to 326 (0.57 per 100) after agency-issued smartphones (RR 3.04, 95% CI 2.44–3.79); audio requests tripled; most requested languages were Spanish (36%), Somali (34%) and Arabic (10%).

papers.title: Extrication after road collisions: an evidence map
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Scoping review
papers.finding: Mapped rescue characteristics studied against morbidity, mortality and physiological deterioration; found inconsistent definitions of entrapment, extrication method and time, and heterogenous outcome reporting limiting synthesis and system-level learning.

papers.title: A US systems approach to MCI triage
papers.journal: The Surgical Clinics of North America
papers.design: Narrative clinical review
papers.finding: Sets out early recognition, resource escalation and dynamic primary/secondary/tertiary triage with retriage, casualty collection and ambulance exchange points, and Incident Command System–structured triage-driven transport.

papers.title: Self-efficacy predicts bystander willingness for CPR
papers.design: Convergent parallel mixed-methods study (SEM plus thematic interviews)
papers.finding: Self-efficacy was the strongest predictor of intention (β 0.515, p<0.001, large effect), attitude smaller (β 0.206) and perceived norms negligible (β 0.094); intention mediated the path to behavioural willingness.

papers.title: Paramedic students learn safety from unsafe events
papers.design: Qualitative descriptive study (conventional content analysis)
papers.finding: Four themes emerged: professional role modelling and feedback, unsafe situations as learning triggers, emotional impact and student vulnerability, and developing patient-safety awareness for future practice.

papers.title: Drowning and trauma lead Swedish mountain deaths
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Descriptive retrospective study (search-and-rescue registry plus autopsy reports)
papers.finding: Drowning (n=7) and traumatic injuries (n=7) were the leading causes of death, then suffocation (4), hypothermia (4), disease (3) and intoxication (1); 25 of 26 were male and 13 died alone.

papers.title: Protocol: climate and emergency dispatch volumes
papers.design: Exploratory retrospective population-based observational protocol (quasi-Poisson, distributed lag nonlinear models)
papers.finding: Protocol only — will assess nonlinear temperature-response relationships, temporal lags and spatial variation in dispatch volumes across Hanover and Brunswick, comparing high-resolution versus station-based exposure data.

papers.title: Updated paediatric traumatic arrest position statement
papers.design: Joint position statement and resource document
papers.finding: Recommendations: promptly identify children who may benefit from trauma-centre transport; treat reversible causes with direct pressure, wound packing and tourniquets, least-invasive airway management, and chest decompression only if thoracic trauma is suspected (no empiric bilateral decompression); compressions and ventilations have a larger role in paediatric than adult traumatic arrest.

papers.title: Choking arrests: ROSC common, survival still poor
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort (CanROC, 2005–2023)
papers.n: 105,178 EMS-treated OHCAs, of which 1,106 obviously FBAO-related
papers.finding: FBAO-related arrests achieved prehospital ROSC more often than presumed cardiac arrests (62.7% vs 37.8%, OR 2.77) but survival to discharge did not differ (10.6% vs 9.0%, p=0.094); within FBAO arrests, survival was 18.1% with prehospital ROSC and 0.8% without, and was associated with younger age (aOR 0.76 per decade), shockable rhythm (aOR 4.76) and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.81 per minute).

papers.title: Traumatic pneumothorax: most EDs don't drain early
papers.design: Two-centre retrospective cohort
papers.n: 339 patients aged 14 and over with traumatic pneumothorax
papers.finding: 231 patients (68.1%) were initially managed without drainage; pneumothorax size >35 mm (aOR 41.0, 95% CI 16.4–102) and haemothorax (aOR 6.3, 95% CI 2.5–15.8) predicted ED-initiated drainage; 22.8% of drained patients had a recorded complication and in-hospital mortality was 5.6%.

papers.title: Studying barriers to trauma triage tool use
papers.design: Qualitative study protocol (phenomenological, CFIR framework)
papers.n: Up to 30 Dublin Fire Brigade responders and managers
papers.finding: Protocol only — semi-structured interviews and focus groups are underway, with results intended to inform Irish trauma triage implementation strategy.

papers.title: Shift work is rough on paramedics' teeth
papers.design: Nationwide cross-sectional online survey
papers.finding: 54.9% reported current or recent dental/oral problems, 20% had no dental check-up in two years, and hygiene-kit availability was strongly associated with daily or more frequent on-duty brushing among 24-hour staff (85% vs 21%); 88–90% were willing to undergo workplace screening.

papers.title: Rescue breaths linked to better paediatric arrest survival
papers.design: Nationwide registry cohort (All-Japan Utstein Registry, 2005–2023)
papers.n: 26,785 children aged ≤17 with OHCA and known bystander CPR
papers.finding: Adjusted CO-CPR probability rose 14.6% → 55.1% (2005–2023) while RB-CPR fell 41.7% → 10.4%; 30-day neurologically favourable survival was 9.5% with CO-CPR and 3.6% with no bystander CPR, with RB-CPR highest

papers.title: Incomplete on-scene care in paediatric cardiac arrest
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort with linked ePCR review (CARES)
papers.n: 176 children <15 with non-traumatic OHCA (156 linked to ePCR)
papers.finding: Adrenaline before transport in 58/143 (41%) non-shockable arrests and fluids in 12 (8%); defibrillation in 11/13 (85%) shockable; median scene time 10 minutes; 10/176 (6%) survived to discharge, 6 (3%) with favourable neurology

papers.title: Blood stored on ambulances stays within limits to day 42
papers.design: Randomised controlled experimental study of blood units (physician-staffed French EMS conditions)
papers.n: 26 leukoreduced RBC units (12 onboard ambulance, 14 blood bank)
papers.finding: All units below the 0.8% haemolysis threshold at day 42, but ambulance storage gave higher haemolysis at day 28 (+0.043 pp) and day 42 (+0.096 pp) and extra microerythrocyte accumulation, mostly between days 28 and 42

papers.title: Blood biomarker assay fits inside an EMS transport window
papers.design: Prospective pilot simulation study
papers.finding: Median teleconsent 2 minutes, device data entry 1 minute, total workflow 6.5 minutes (IQR 5–7); over 90% reported sufficient training and all indicated willingness to adopt

papers.title: Five dispatch codes drive a third of prehospital blood use
papers.design: Retrospective prehospital blood database analysis
papers.finding: Top five MPDS codes (high-mechanism crash, penetrating central wounds, auto-versus-pedestrian, entrapment, auto-versus-bike/motorcycle) accounted for 29% of units; four medical haemorrhage/arrest codes accounted for a further 11% (51 patients)

papers.title: Machine-learning OHCA survival model from 370 patients
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective prediction-model study (Hangzhou)
papers.n: 370 adults with non-traumatic OHCA (114 achieved ROSC)
papers.finding: Test-set ROC-AUC 0.9815 and PR-AUC 0.9515, Brier score 0.127; key features were on-site defibrillation, cumulative adrenaline dose, time to CPR, time to intubation, PCO2 and time to IV access

papers.title: More arrests, more TORs during the pandemic years
papers.design: Retrospective observational cohort
papers.finding: OHCA incidence increased across all seasons (peak fall 2020); termination-of-resuscitation rate 56.6% → 61.2% (P=.01); scene times 24.4 → 26.1 minutes (P=.04) with transport times unchanged

papers.title: Smoking flags wider heart risk in EMS staff
papers.design: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary recertification survey
papers.n: 7,703 EMTs, advanced EMTs and paramedics with complete data (of 36,436 respondents)
papers.finding: Current smokers (6.0%) had adjusted mLE7 score −6.02 (95% CI −7.63 to −4.41) and aOR 0.37 for ideal cardiovascular health versus never smokers; former smokers intermediate (aOR 0.73)

papers.title: Debriefing works, but nobody reports it the same way
papers.design: Scoping review (Arksey and O'Malley framework, PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 18 studies from 974 records, mostly US and quantitative
papers.finding: Guided debriefing in 15 studies and tool/technology-assisted in 3; debriefing associated with improvements in technical performance, communication, teamwork, clinical reasoning and reflective practice, with inconsistent reporting of facilitation, structure and outcomes

papers.title: Heat-alert days bring more ambulance dispatches, not fewer
papers.design: National daily time-series analysis with matched days and conditional Poisson regression
papers.n: 2,715 heat-alert days 2020–2023, 1,310 matched pairs (2,620 observation days)
papers.finding: Emergency ambulance dispatches on heat-alert days rose all-cause by 3.11% (95% CI 1.74–4.50), genitourinary by 5.82% and heatstroke by 31.1% (95% CI 21.2–41.8); no significant mortality association

papers.title: Community paramedicine programs can't agree on names
papers.design: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews
papers.n: 23 of 58 identified expanded-EMS programs in Ohio
papers.finding: Inconsistent use and interpretation of MIH, CP and MIH-CP terms; 1 in 4 programs used alternative terminology (e.g. neighbourhood paramedic, EMS outreach), attributed to variable definitions and limited stakeholder understanding

papers.title: Flipped classroom beats lectures for ECG skills
papers.design: Quasi-experimental interventional study with pretest-posttest design
papers.n: Prehospital emergency personnel in Iran, 2025 (sample size not reported in abstract)
papers.finding: Flipped-classroom group scored significantly higher at two weeks (mean 6.84, p=0.002) and one month after intervention; groups were equivalent at baseline (p=0.10)

papers.title: Most prehospital tourniquets unjustified, few harmed
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre trauma registry chart review
papers.finding: 69.4% of tourniquets were unjustified; justified cases were more severely injured and more often needed surgery or transfusion, but unjustified placement showed no difference in mortality, compartment syndrome or nerve palsy

papers.title: Gastric distension after OHCA similar across airways
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre CT volumetry cohort
papers.n: 120 OHCA patients with CT within 180 minutes (of 255 screened)
papers.finding: Median total gastric volume 594 mL; no significant gastric-volume difference between tracheal (n=87) and supraglottic (n=28) groups; CT-defined aspiration numerically higher with supraglottic airways (78.6% vs 57.5%, OR 2.7, p=0.071)

papers.title: DNAR directives missing when crews arrive
papers.design: Mixed-methods survey with reflexive thematic analysis
papers.finding: 54.0% had encountered CPA with DNAR; among them 80% performed basic life support and 91% transported; four themes centred on inadequate DNAR decision-making processes, absent accommodating systems, scope-of-practice conflicts with patient wishes, and emotional burden

papers.title: Small-group resuscitation training: what works?
papers.design: Systematic review (seven RCTs including one cluster-randomised, one non-randomised curriculum evaluation) with narrative synthesis
papers.n: 8 studies of resuscitation training in groups of varying sizes
papers.finding: Immediate post-course CPR performance and test scores were similar across group sizes; smaller instructor-led groups offered more hands-on practice, interaction, questions and individualised feedback; instructor error detection declined when supervising more than six learners in one BLS simulation trial; no patient or clinical outcomes were reported.

papers.title: Measuring CPR ventilation rate with capnography
papers.design: Cohort study with capnographic breath detection, physician-staffed mobile emergency unit
papers.n: 83 CPR segments from 75 adult OHCA resuscitation attempts
papers.finding: Moderate-to-good agreement with independent detectors (ICC 0.72–0.82, limits of agreement ±6.8 breaths/min) but no association between ventilation rate and ROSC (OR 1.09 per 2 breaths/min, 95% CI 0.91–1.30)

papers.title: AED data retrieval is fragmented across Europe
papers.design: Cross-sectional observational survey
papers.n: 60 AEDs from 24 manufacturers in four European countries
papers.finding: Transitional interfaces in 41.6% of devices and legacy interfaces in 21.7%; free software available for 43.3%, paid software required for 26.7% and distributor access for 13.3%

papers.title: Bystander CPR defines the prehospital OHCA profile
papers.design: Nationwide registry cohort with latent class analysis
papers.finding: Bystander CPR was associated with survival to discharge (17.7% vs 10.0%; aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.52–1.71), ED ROSC (aOR 1.11) and favourable neurological outcome (aOR 2.23, 95% CI 2.04–2.44); call-to-ED time ≤20 min did not separate the latent classes, and ED arrivals within 20 min fell from 28.8% to 5.6% while bystander CPR rose from 66.3% to 75.2%

papers.title: Hands-on CPR training beats video for teens
papers.design: Randomised pretest–posttest controlled trial
papers.finding: Both groups improved in knowledge and self-confidence over time (p < 0.001); the simulation group scored significantly higher than the video group on knowledge, CPR skill and self-confidence immediately after training

papers.title: Liberal ambulance fluids did not reduce sepsis mortality
papers.design: Multicentre 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial (4 Ontario paramedic services)
papers.finding: Hospital mortality 18.0% with liberal fluids (median 1500 mL) versus 18.3% with usual care (median 500 mL), RR 0.98 (95% CI 0.80–1.20); all 17 secondary outcomes similar.

papers.title: Ambulance antibiotics gave no survival benefit in sepsis
papers.design: Multicentre 2×2 factorial randomised placebo-controlled trial (4 Ontario paramedic services)
papers.finding: Hospital mortality 18.0% with ambulance IM ceftriaxone versus 18.4% with placebo, RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.81–1.17); all 17 secondary outcomes similar.

papers.title: Paragliding festival injuries cluster at landing
papers.design: Retrospective review of operational and prehospital records from a 2-day mountain paragliding festival (brief report)
papers.finding: 10 of 13 injuries (76.9%) occurred during landing versus 1 during takeoff; lower-limb trauma predominated; 8 patients went by ground ambulance and 1 deceased pilot required helicopter-assisted recovery.

papers.title: Shockable rhythms decay fast in untreated arrest
papers.design: Systematic review (PRISMA) of cohorts, registries, waveform analyses and RCTs
papers.n: 38 studies, more than 262,700 adult OHCA cases
papers.finding: Median initial shockable rhythm prevalence 33.5% in unselected cohorts; increasing time-to-defibrillation was consistently associated with falling shockable-rhythm prevalence, lower defibrillation success, less ROSC and worse survival

papers.title: Simulated prehospital eCPR shows large time savings
papers.design: Prospective observational simulation study within a hospital-based eCPR programme
papers.n: 23 simulated prehospital cases vs 25 in-hospital eCPR patients
papers.finding: Call-to-decision 18 (SD 5) vs 49 minutes; estimated call-to-ECMO-flow shorter in the prehospital arm, assuming 20 minutes of on-scene cannulation

papers.title: Heat and ozone together raise cardiac arrest risk
papers.design: Nationwide time-stratified case-crossover analysis with random-effects meta-pooling
papers.finding: Above a ~60 ppb ozone threshold, each 10 ppb rise at extreme heat (99th percentile temperature) was associated with RR 1.04 (95% CI 1.03–1.05), with synergistic interaction on both additive and multiplicative scales

papers.title: Recorded burn cooling varied by family citizenship
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre descriptive cohort
papers.finding: Cooling recorded for 79.1% of Italian vs 61.2% of non-Italian records (difference −17.8 pp, 95% CI −28.0 to −7.9); adjusted odds ratios 2.04 for no first aid and 3.15 for remedies in non-Italian records

papers.title: Where transfer delay hits paediatric testicular torsion
papers.design: Retrospective cohort with parametric g-computation counterfactual modelling
papers.finding: Median prehospital time 28.5 h in transferred boys vs 9.5 h direct (adjusted time ratio 1.75, 95% CI 1.33–2.31); under a 100% reduction scenario nonviability fell 42.1%→34.7% and orchiectomy 33.4%→27.3%

papers.title: Gen Z learning evidence skips paramedicine
papers.journal: Journal of Medical Education and Curricular Development
papers.design: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR, Joanna Briggs framework)
papers.n: 8 studies across four professions; none in paramedicine
papers.finding: Three themes — technology-supported learning preferences, active and interactive approaches, and autonomy-motivation-feedback; no eligible paramedicine studies identified
